name: rhetorical_figures
description: Working handlist of rhetorical schemes and tropes at Lanham/Silva Rhetoricae scale: repetition, balance, omission, amplification, word order, wordplay and word-form, metaphor and metonymy families, irony, definition and division, question and address, description, argumentation, emotional appeal, and the classical vices of style.

repetition_figures.name: anaphora
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of the same word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses or sentences.
repetition_figures.example: We tried the front door. We tried the window. We tried the neighbor with the spare key.
repetition_figures.effect: Builds insistence and drumbeat rhythm; makes a list feel like an accumulation of pressure.
repetition_figures.register: formal to neutral; oratory, argument, and heightened narration
repetition_figures.caution: The single most overused figure in machine-generated prose. One anaphoric run per chapter, and never in threes back to back.

repetition_figures.name: epistrophe
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of the same word or phrase at the end of successive clauses or sentences.
repetition_figures.example: The contract said nothing about the road. The survey said nothing about the road. The seller, when asked, said nothing about the road.
repetition_figures.effect: Drives the emphasis onto the repeated term and lets it land as a verdict.
repetition_figures.register: formal to neutral; argument and closing passages
repetition_figures.caution: Heavier than anaphora because the reader waits for the thud each time; two members is usually enough.

repetition_figures.name: symploce
repetition_figures.definition: Anaphora and epistrophe together: successive clauses share both an opening and a closing phrase.
repetition_figures.example: Who signed the waiver? The contractor signed the waiver. Who read the waiver? Nobody read the waiver.
repetition_figures.effect: Frames a variable inside a fixed structure so the one changing word carries all the weight.
repetition_figures.caution: Highly conspicuous; a reader notices the machinery before the meaning if it runs past three members.

repetition_figures.name: anadiplosis
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of the word that ends one clause at the beginning of the next.
repetition_figures.example: The delay cost us the quarter, and the quarter cost us the client.
repetition_figures.effect: Welds two clauses into a causal chain and slows the sentence at the hinge.

repetition_figures.name: gradatio
repetition_figures.definition: A chain of anadiplosis in which each repeated term steps the thought up to a culminating point.
repetition_figures.example: Neglect breeds delay, delay breeds excuses, excuses breed the habit of never finishing anything.
repetition_figures.effect: Makes an inference feel inevitable by walking the reader up it one rung at a time.
repetition_figures.caution: Reads as sermonizing if the rungs are not genuinely consecutive; do not fake the links.

repetition_figures.name: epizeuxis
repetition_figures.definition: Immediate repetition of a word with nothing intervening.
repetition_figures.example: It was cold. Cold like the inside of a bell.
repetition_figures.effect: Registers raw intensity or shock, as if the speaker's control has slipped for a beat.
repetition_figures.caution: In exposition it reads as theatrical; reserve it for moments where control genuinely slips.

repetition_figures.name: diacope
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a word broken up by one or a few intervening words.
repetition_figures.example: Alone in the house, alone in the dark, she counted the furnace clicks.
repetition_figures.effect: Holds a word in the ear while the sentence turns around it.

repetition_figures.name: epanalepsis
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition at the end of a clause of the word that began it.
repetition_figures.example: Money follows attention, and attention follows money.
repetition_figures.effect: Closes the clause on itself, producing a sealed, proverbial finish.

repetition_figures.name: polyptoton
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of words derived from the same root in different grammatical forms.
repetition_figures.example: The judge judged, and the judgment was judged in turn.
repetition_figures.effect: Turns a single idea over through its parts of speech, showing its reach without new vocabulary.
repetition_figures.caution: Can tip into cleverness for its own sake; keep to two or three forms.

repetition_figures.name: antanaclasis
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a word in a different sense from its first use.
repetition_figures.example: If we do not hang together, we shall hang separately.
repetition_figures.effect: Pivots on a pun to make a serious point land as wit.

repetition_figures.name: antistasis
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a word in a sense directly contrary to its first use.
repetition_figures.example: A free market is only free for those who can afford to leave it.
repetition_figures.effect: Exposes an equivocation by forcing both senses into the same sentence.

repetition_figures.name: ploce
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a word within the same clause or sentence with a shift of emphasis or connotation rather than of dictionary sense.
repetition_figures.example: He was a doctor, but not a doctor you would let near a wound.
repetition_figures.effect: Draws a fine distinction between the name of a thing and the reality of it.

repetition_figures.name: diaphora
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a name so that the second use denotes the qualities the name has come to stand for.
repetition_figures.example: Boys will be boys, and auditors will be auditors.
repetition_figures.effect: Compresses a whole characterization into a tautology the reader is invited to unpack.

repetition_figures.name: conduplicatio
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a key word from a preceding clause at the start of the following one, for amplification or emotional emphasis.
repetition_figures.example: They promised transparency. Transparency, from an office that shreds its own minutes.
repetition_figures.effect: Seizes the word and makes it the subject of the sentence that follows, often with scorn.

repetition_figures.name: epanodos
repetition_figures.definition: Naming a series and then taking up its members again in reverse order to treat each in turn.
repetition_figures.example: The plan needed money and nerve: nerve nobody had, money nobody would lend.
repetition_figures.effect: Signals orderly coverage while giving the last-named item the emphatic first slot.

repetition_figures.name: epimone
repetition_figures.definition: Persistent repetition of a phrase or question at intervals through a passage.
repetition_figures.example: And still no one had called the inspector. Three months of memos, two site visits, a partial collapse. And still no one had called the inspector.
repetition_figures.effect: Turns a phrase into a refrain that measures the passage and indicts by recurrence.
repetition_figures.caution: Needs real interval between returns; back-to-back it becomes nagging rather than haunting.

repetition_figures.name: tautotes
repetition_figures.definition: Wearisome repetition of the same word in the same form throughout a passage.
repetition_figures.example: The report reports what the reporting officer reported to the reporting committee.
repetition_figures.effect: Almost always a fault, but deployable to mimic bureaucratic deadness.
repetition_figures.caution: Only ever use in voice; unintentional tautotes is the commonest symptom of an unedited draft.

repetition_figures.name: homoioptoton
repetition_figures.definition: Successive members ending in words of the same case or inflectional form.
repetition_figures.example: By training, by temperament, by long habit of caution, he refused.
repetition_figures.effect: Gives parallel members an audible click of closure.

repetition_figures.name: homoioteleuton
repetition_figures.definition: Successive members ending in similar sounds, producing near-rhyme across clauses.
repetition_figures.example: The funding was late, the schedule was tight, the outcome was slight.
repetition_figures.effect: Binds the members by ear; at the limit it turns prose into jingle.
repetition_figures.caution: Accidental rhyme in prose reads as sing-song; keep it deliberate and brief.

repetition_figures.name: paromoiosis
repetition_figures.definition: Parallelism of members whose corresponding parts also correspond in sound.
repetition_figures.example: Slow to promise, slow to please.
repetition_figures.effect: Fuses structural and sonic symmetry so the pair feels like a maxim.

repetition_figures.name: mesodiplosis
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a word or phrase in the middle of successive clauses.
repetition_figures.example: The tenants were told, quietly, to wait; the inspectors were told, quietly, to look elsewhere.
repetition_figures.effect: Puts the recurring term at the sentence's soft center, where it works by insinuation.

repetition_figures.name: mesarchia
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of the same word or phrase at the beginning and in the middle of successive clauses.
repetition_figures.example: Nothing moved, nothing at all, in the yard; nothing moved, nothing at all, on the road.
repetition_figures.effect: Doubles the anchor points of a parallel structure, producing an incantatory pulse.
repetition_figures.caution: Very ornate; a whole paragraph of it reads as liturgy.

repetition_figures.name: mesoteleuton
repetition_figures.definition: Repetition of a word or phrase in the middle and at the end of successive clauses.
repetition_figures.example: They wanted proof, hard proof; we offered notes, not proof.
repetition_figures.effect: Sets up a mid-clause echo that the clause ending then confirms.

repetition_figures.name: scesis onomaton
repetition_figures.definition: A string of successive expressions that restate a single idea in different words.
repetition_figures.example: He stalled, he temporized, he found one more thing to check first.
repetition_figures.effect: Presses one idea from several angles until it is unavoidable.
repetition_figures.caution: The line between amplification and padding is thin; each restatement must add a shade the last one lacked.

repetition_figures.name: figura etymologica
repetition_figures.definition: Pairing a verb with a noun built from the same root, so the object echoes the action that governs it.
repetition_figures.example: He dreamed the dream his father had dreamed, and woke to the same unpaid bill.
repetition_figures.effect: Tightens a clause into a closed circuit and gives an ordinary verb the weight of a formula.
repetition_figures.register: neutral to formal; scripture-flavored narration, aphorism
repetition_figures.caution: Reads as translationese if the root pair is not already idiomatic in English.

repetition_figures.name: repetend
repetition_figures.definition: A word or phrase brought back at irregular intervals through a passage without the fixed placement of a refrain.
repetition_figures.example: The word in the file was routine. Routine inspection, routine variance, routine sign-off, and then a routine funeral.
repetition_figures.effect: Plants a term early and lets each return collect the meaning of everything since.
repetition_figures.caution: Needs at least one return that changes the term's value, or it is only a verbal tic.

repetition_figures.name: incremental repetition
repetition_figures.definition: Repeating a line or clause with one element changed each time, so the sense advances by a single step per pass.
repetition_figures.example: She asked the clerk. She asked the clerk's supervisor. She asked the supervisor's supervisor, who asked her to put it in writing.
repetition_figures.effect: Gives narrative motion the shape of a ballad: the same ground, one field farther each time.
repetition_figures.register: neutral; folk narrative, reportage, oral-derived prose
repetition_figures.caution: Ballad meter is contagious; three passes is usually the ceiling in prose.

repetition_figures.name: inclusio
repetition_figures.definition: Framing a passage by repeating at its close the word, image, or clause that opened it.
repetition_figures.example: The road ended at the quarry. Everything the county built for the next forty years began there, and every hearing about it ended at the quarry.
repetition_figures.effect: Closes a unit audibly, so a reader feels the paragraph or chapter finish rather than merely stop.
repetition_figures.register: neutral to formal; scripture, essay, chapter architecture
repetition_figures.caution: Too neat a bracket makes an argument feel settled when it is not; leave the frame open if the question is.

repetition_figures.name: variatio
repetition_figures.definition: Deliberate variation of a repeated element — word, construction, or clause length — so that a pattern is felt without becoming mechanical.
repetition_figures.example: The first inspector wrote it down. The second logged it. The third, who had been there longest, said nothing to anyone.
repetition_figures.effect: Keeps the pleasure of a pattern while removing the metronome from it.
repetition_figures.caution: Varying the word for a thing that must stay identifiable is the vice of elegant variation, not variatio.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: isocolon
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Successive clauses of equal length and matching grammatical structure.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: He kept the books. She kept the peace.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Confers a machined symmetry that makes assertions feel weighed and equal.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: Sustained isocolon flattens argument into slogan and is a strong signature of generated prose.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: parison
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Correspondence of grammatical structure between successive members, without requiring equal length.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: To draft is to guess; to revise is to find out what you guessed.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Lets the reader compare content directly because the frames are identical.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: bicolon
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: A two-membered balanced construction, the smallest parallel unit.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: Cheap to build, ruinous to maintain.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Sets two things against each other with no third to soften the pairing.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: tricolon
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Three parallel members in sequence.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: It was underfunded, understaffed, and, by the second winter, unheated.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Gives the sense of completeness that three items produce in English rhythm.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: The default cadence of machine prose. If every paragraph has a triad, cut two of every three.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: tricolon crescens
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: A tricolon whose members grow successively longer.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: He lost the deposit, the lease, and every friend who had signed as guarantor.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Builds momentum toward the longest member, which lands as the climax.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: Very hard to use twice in a page without the second one sounding like a parody of the first.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: tetracolon
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Four parallel members in sequence.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: Survey it, price it, permit it, and only then promise it.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Breaks the expected triad, producing a procedural, list-like weight.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: antithesis
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Figure sense: juxtaposition of contrasting ideas in parallel grammatical form. Distinct from the RST relation of the same name, which concerns which of two spans the reader is meant to prefer.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: The policy was generous in wording and stingy in practice.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Sharpens a claim by giving the reader its opposite in the same breath.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: The not-X-but-Y frame is the most conspicuous AI tell in modern prose; earn each contrast or drop it.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: antitheton
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Proof or argument constructed out of opposites, treated as a figure of thought rather than of words.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: If secrecy served the public, the file would have been sealed by a public vote.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Forces the reader to accept a conclusion by eliminating its contrary.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: antimetabole
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Repetition of the same words in reversed grammatical order.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: We do not fund what we measure; we measure what we fund.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Produces the sensation of a proof by symmetry, whether or not one has occurred.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: Nearly irresistible and nearly always shallow; use once per book and only when the reversal is true.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: chiasmus
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Inverted parallel structure in which the second member mirrors the order of the first without repeating its words.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: The wealthy arrived early and left unnoticed; unnoticed and late, the rest arrived.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Closes a pattern by turning it inside out, giving a sense of completed symmetry.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: Fussy in plain exposition; the mirror has to mean something, not merely look tidy. Note the standard treatment: antimetabole is the species of chiasmus in which the mirrored terms are repeated verbatim, so every antimetabole is a chiasmus and most chiasmus is not antimetabole.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: syncrisis
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Comparison of contrary things in parallel members.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: The one built slowly and sold late; the other built fast and sold everything twice.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Lets two cases be judged against each other without an explicit verdict.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: synoeciosis
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: The yoking of contraries so that both are asserted at once as a single composed truth.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: It was a rescue that ruined them and a ruin that saved the town.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Holds a genuine contradiction open instead of resolving it.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: oxymoron
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: A compact phrase joining two contradictory terms.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: a generous cruelty
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Compresses a paradox into two words and makes the reader do the reconciling.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: Most oxymorons in circulation are dead; a fresh one requires a real contradiction, not a fashionable pairing.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: paradox
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: A statement that appears self-contradictory yet resolves into sense on reflection.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: The cheapest way to run the plant was to shut it for a year.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Arrests the reader at the apparent contradiction and buys attention for the explanation.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: comparatio
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Extended, point-by-point comparison of two persons, things, or courses of action.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: Where the first firm audited quarterly, the second audited when sued; where the first published its errors, the second published its awards.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Builds a verdict cumulatively out of matched particulars.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: synonymous parallelism
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Two balanced members that restate one idea in different words, the second adding force rather than new information.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: The river took the bridge; the water carried off the road.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Doubles a statement's weight and slows the reader at the point of emphasis.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: Sounds liturgical fast; in argument, readers hear the second member as padding unless it sharpens.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: synthetic parallelism
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Balanced members in which the second completes, extends, or specifies the first rather than restating or opposing it.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: They filed the permit in March; by June the pond behind the culvert had a name.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Gets the cadence of parallelism while still advancing the argument.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: climactic parallelism
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: Parallel members in which each picks up part of the previous member and carries it one stage further to a peak.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: They knew the culvert was small. They knew a small culvert floods. They knew it floods the school.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Builds to a landing point that feels earned because the reader climbed each step.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: The last step must be the largest, or the ladder collapses into anticlimax.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: priamel
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: A list of alternatives set out only to be dismissed in favor of the final one, which is the speaker's real subject.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: Some counties are known for their courthouse, some for their fairground, some for a governor born in a farmhouse; this one is known for the water it could not hold.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Uses the discarded options as a frame that makes the chosen one look inevitable.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: The rejected members must be plausible; a straw list makes the conclusion look pre-cooked.

balance_and_antithesis_figures.name: antapodosis
balance_and_antithesis_figures.definition: The answering half of a comparison — the clause that supplies the 'so' to a preceding 'as' or 'just as'.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.example: As a hairline crack takes a season to open, so the finding took a season to reach anyone who could act on it.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.effect: Completes a simile as a formal structure, which gives it the authority of a proposition.
balance_and_antithesis_figures.register: formal; scripture-flavored prose, argument, epic simile
balance_and_antithesis_figures.caution: If the answering clause repeats the first in different nouns, the figure is decoration with no cargo.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: asyndeton
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Omission of conjunctions between coordinated words, phrases, or clauses.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: He signed, he paid, he left.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Speeds the line and suggests the list could continue past what is shown.
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: Paired with a triad it becomes the stock cadence of generated summary prose.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: brachylogia
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Asyndeton applied between single words rather than clauses.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Cold, wet, unlit, unsafe.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Produces a clipped inventory that feels like evidence rather than description.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: ellipsis
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Omission of a word or words that the reader supplies from context.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Some brought tools; others, only opinions.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Tightens the sentence and rewards the reader for completing it.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: zeugma
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: One governing word yoked to two or more others, at least one of which fits awkwardly or unequally.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: The committee raised objections and, eventually, the roof.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Yokes unlike things by grammar, producing wit or strain by the mismatch.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: syllepsis
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: One word governing two others in two different senses at once.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: She took her coat, her severance, and her time.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Delivers a pun structurally rather than by sound, and reads as dry rather than jokey.
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: One per essay; a second announces that the writer is pleased with the first.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: prozeugma
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Zeugma in which the governing verb appears in the first clause and is understood in those that follow.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: The auditor found the ledger; the clerk, the missing page; the widow, nothing at all.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Keeps a long parallel series moving by refusing to restate the verb.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: mesozeugma
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Zeugma in which the governing verb stands in a middle clause and serves those on either side.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: The first witness and, under oath, the second contradicted the third.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Balances the sentence around its verb rather than beginning or ending on it.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: hypozeugma
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Zeugma in which the governing verb comes only in the final clause.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: The tenants, the inspectors, the man who wrote the original permit, all lied.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Suspends the sentence until the last word, which then discharges the whole series.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: diazeugma
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: One subject governing a succession of different verbs.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: The company denied, delayed, appealed, settled, and denied again.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Keeps a single agent onstage while the actions accumulate against them.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: aposiopesis
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Figure sense: breaking off in the middle of a sentence and leaving the rest unsaid, as a deliberate rhetorical gesture.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: If the inspector had walked ten feet farther that morning—
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Hands the unsaid to the reader, who supplies something worse than the writer could.
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: Once it is a gesture; twice it is a tic, and in exposition it reads as evasion.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: anapodoton
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Omission of the main clause of a conditional or correlative sentence, the sense being obvious.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: If you think that was the expensive part.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Implies the consequence by refusing to state it, which reads as confident and dry.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: anantapodoton
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Omission of one member of a correlative pair, so that the answering term never arrives.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Sometimes the money is there and the will is not.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Leaves an expected counterweight missing, which the reader feels as an absence.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: apo koinou
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: A word or phrase shared by two clauses, belonging grammatically to both.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: There was a man came to the door said nothing.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Splices clauses at speed; in narration it reads as spoken, unpunctuated thought.
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: Reads as an error unless the surrounding voice is clearly vernacular.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: brevitas
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Expression of a matter in the fewest possible words.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: He came, he saw, he conquered.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Signals mastery of the material by refusing to elaborate.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: articulus
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Phrasing by single words set off with commas, each pressed forward without connectives.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Cut. Weld. Grind. Inspect.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Chops the rhythm into strokes, imitating action or urgency.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: emphasis
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Implying more than the words state, so the reader infers the unsaid charge.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: He was, in those years, remarkably fortunate at auction.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Lets an accusation be made without being made, which is harder to rebut.
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: In nonfiction the unsaid claim still needs to be true and defensible.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: syllogismus
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Implying a conclusion by presenting the telling detail and leaving the inference to the audience.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: The safety officer resigned in March. The revised inspection form is dated April.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Makes the reader draw the damning conclusion, which is more persuasive than being told it.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: percursio
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Running rapidly over many matters in the briefest possible mention.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Set aside the permits, the soil study, the two resignations, the loan.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Conveys abundance without cost in space, and implies the writer could dwell but will not.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: abbreviatio
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: The deliberate practice of compressing material — the medieval counterpart to copia — by cutting, summarizing, and implying rather than stating.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Six months of hearings, three consultants, and one exhausted clerk produced the sentence: the culvert stays.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Buys pace and signals that the writer knows what does not matter.
omission_and_brevity_figures.register: neutral; all prose, especially narrative nonfiction
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: Compression that skips the causal link reads as an assertion the reader is expected to take on faith.

omission_and_brevity_figures.name: epitrochasmus
omission_and_brevity_figures.definition: Running rapidly through a series of points, touching each in a word or two and stopping at none.
omission_and_brevity_figures.example: Permits, waivers, the second survey, the missing gauge, the retirement party — all of it fits in a paragraph, and all of it mattered.
omission_and_brevity_figures.effect: Conveys abundance and haste at once; the reader feels the volume of material without reading it.
omission_and_brevity_figures.caution: A reader who wanted one of those items will notice you skipped it; use it only for the genuinely subordinate.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: polysyndeton
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Deliberate use of more conjunctions than syntax requires.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: There was mud and rain and a generator that would not start and no one who knew how.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Slows the list to a trudge and makes each item weigh the same as the last.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Strongly marked; in analytic prose it reads as costume.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: congeries
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Heaping up of words or phrases of related meaning without ordered progression.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: Notes, receipts, drafts, photographs, a wallet, a bus ticket, the whole silt of a life.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Creates the impression of overwhelming quantity by sheer accumulation.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: accumulatio
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Gathering points already made and presenting them together in a forceful summary.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: A missing permit, an unqualified crew, a falsified sign-off, a night shift with no supervisor: this is what the company calls an accident.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Converts scattered evidence into a single indictment at the moment of summing up.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: auxesis
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Magnifying a thing by naming it with a weightier word than it strictly deserves.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: He called the missing invoice a catastrophe.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Inflates the subject, either to persuade or, when the inflation is visible, to mock.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Unearned auxesis is the engine of purple prose; the reader deflates it faster than you inflate it.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: incrementum
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Arrangement of a series so that each item is stronger than the one before.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: It cost him the deposit, then the business, then the marriage.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Gives the series a ladder shape so the last item feels like a destination.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: anticlimax
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Arrangement in which the final item drops abruptly below the level of those preceding.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: He risked his savings, his reputation, and his Tuesday evenings.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Punctures a build deliberately; used unintentionally it is a classic failure of tone.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Only funny when the drop is obviously chosen; otherwise it reads as a lost thread.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: expolitio
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Dwelling on one point by restating it in varied words, forms, and illustrations.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: The road was not repaired. It was patched. Gravel was pushed into the hole and rolled flat, and the hole came back in April.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Keeps a single idea in view long enough for it to sink in without literal repetition.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: The most common source of bloat; each turn must add information, not decoration.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: commoratio
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Dwelling on or returning to the strongest point of one's case.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: Everything else is detail. The bolt was never torqued. Whatever the schedule said, whatever the weather did, the bolt was never torqued.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Refuses to let the argument drift from the fact that decides it.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: amplificatio
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: The general enlargement of a subject to make it seem greater or more consequential than a plain statement would.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: This was not one missed inspection but a decade of them, spread across four counties and two administrations.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Scales a particular up into a pattern the reader is asked to weigh.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Scaling up must survive fact-checking; amplification that outruns the evidence discredits the rest.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: epexegesis
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Adding a word or clause that explains or specifies what precedes.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: They chose the cheaper fix, which is to say they chose the one that would fail after the warranty.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Lets the writer restate in plainer or sharper terms without abandoning the first formulation.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: epitasis
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Adding a concluding sentence that presses home and intensifies what has just been said.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: The fund was exhausted by March. It had been exhausted by March in each of the four preceding years.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Puts a second, heavier weight on a point the reader had already accepted.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: pleonasm
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Use of more words than are needed to convey the sense, whether as fault or as deliberate fullness.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: He saw it with his own eyes.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Slows and solemnizes; in speech it carries emphasis, in exposition usually only fat.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Nearly always cuttable in prose; keep only when the redundancy is doing rhetorical work.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: tautology
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Restating the same idea in different words as though it were a further claim.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: The outcome was unavoidable and could not have been prevented.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Usually a vice; in dialogue it characterizes a speaker padding for authority.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: A leading marker of unedited or machine-smoothed prose; hunt it in revision.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: syntheton
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Joining two words with a conjunction where custom has fused them into a single expression.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: law and order; wear and tear; safe and sound
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Reaches for a ready-made pair that carries a whole attitude with it.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Most synthetons are dead idiom; a fresh pair works, a stock one costs you a sentence.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: hendiadys
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Expressing a single complex idea by two nouns joined with a conjunction instead of a noun and its modifier.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: He spoke with heat and haste, rather than with hasty heat.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Separates a quality from its noun so both stand as equals, which slows and dignifies the phrase.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: hendiatris
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Expressing one idea through three coordinate terms.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: Wind, wire, and winter did the rest.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Distributes a single notion across three names so it feels comprehensive.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: synonymia
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Amplifying by supplying a series of synonyms for the same term.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: It was a delay, a postponement, a deferral, an indefinite putting-off.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Circles a word until the exact shade the writer wants comes into focus.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Thesaurus prose; three near-identical words is padding unless the differences are the point.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: correctio
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Withdrawing or amending what was just said in favor of a stronger or more exact formulation.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: It was a mistake. No: it was a decision, made twice, in writing.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Stages the writer's thinking in real time, which reads as scrupulous and raises the stakes of the correction.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: A favorite trick of persuasive prose and easy to fake; if the first version was never meant, cut it.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: copia
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: The Renaissance principle of abundance: the trained ability to expand a single thought into many varied forms of expression.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: The gauge failed. The gauge stopped reporting. The instrument that was supposed to tell the county the pond was rising told it nothing at all.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Turns one sentence into a paragraph and one paragraph into a chapter, on demand.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Copia is a reserve to draw on, not a target; unearned abundance is what readers call padding.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: anesis
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Adding a closing clause that diminishes the effect of everything before it.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: He had the training, the authority, the funding, and eleven days left before retirement.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Deflates a build on purpose, usually to ironic or elegiac effect.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: One per scene; repeated, it teaches the reader to discount every build you make.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: epic catalogue
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: An extended, formally ordered list of persons, places, or things given at length for its own accumulating weight.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: From the north townships: two graders, one loader, four men who had done this before. From the river road: nothing, because the river road was gone.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Makes scale physical — the reader tires of the list the way the participants tired of the work.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Only earns its length if the items differ; twenty interchangeable entries is a spreadsheet.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: litany
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Accumulation in a fixed liturgical shape: a repeated frame with one variable slot, run past the point of information into incantation.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: For the culvert, no funds. For the survey, no funds. For the siren on the school roof, no funds.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Converts a list into a rite; the reader stops counting items and starts feeling the pattern.
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: The most conspicuous machine in the toolbox, and the fastest route to unearned solemnity.

amplification_and_addition_figures.name: metaphrasis
amplification_and_addition_figures.definition: Restating a passage in different words at similar length, as an exercise or as a way of making a difficult source usable.
amplification_and_addition_figures.example: The statute says a variance may issue on a showing of practical difficulty. In plain terms: if the rule is inconvenient, ask to be excused from it.
amplification_and_addition_figures.effect: Puts a source and its meaning side by side so the reader can check the writer's reading.
amplification_and_addition_figures.register: neutral to formal; exposition, legal and technical writing
amplification_and_addition_figures.caution: Paraphrase that improves the original's argument is a form of misquotation.

word_order_figures.name: anastrophe
word_order_figures.definition: Departure from normal word order, typically by placing a modifier or object before what it governs.
word_order_figures.example: Patience he had none.
word_order_figures.effect: Throws stress onto the fronted element and gives the clause an archaic formality.
word_order_figures.caution: Two in a page and the voice starts to sound like a translation of an epic.

word_order_figures.name: hyperbaton
word_order_figures.definition: Separation of words that belong together by the interposition of other words.
word_order_figures.example: This, of all the excuses offered that year, was the least convincing.
word_order_figures.effect: Suspends the sense across the interruption, which builds pressure toward the resolution.

word_order_figures.name: hypallage
word_order_figures.definition: Transfer of a modifier from the word it logically qualifies to a neighboring one.
word_order_figures.example: the sleepless corridor
word_order_figures.effect: Smuggles an atmosphere into a noun that cannot literally hold it.
word_order_figures.caution: Charming once, mannered on repetition; a page of restless doors and anxious lamps is parody.

word_order_figures.name: parenthesis
word_order_figures.definition: Insertion of a grammatically independent remark into the body of a sentence.
word_order_figures.example: The plan (nobody has ever explained who wrote it) called for two inspections a year.
word_order_figures.effect: Lets a second voice or an aside interrupt without breaking the sentence's spine.
word_order_figures.caution: Heavy parenthesis fragments attention; if the aside matters, give it a sentence.

word_order_figures.name: parembole
word_order_figures.definition: An inserted remark that, unlike ordinary parenthesis, bears directly on the subject of the sentence it interrupts.
word_order_figures.example: The contractor, and this is the point that the inquiry never pursued, had signed the same waiver twice.
word_order_figures.effect: Slips the crucial fact into the least emphatic position, which can read as either candor or cunning.

word_order_figures.name: apposition
word_order_figures.definition: Placing a noun phrase beside another to identify or characterize it.
word_order_figures.example: The foreman, a man who had never signed anything in his life, signed.
word_order_figures.effect: Adds identification and judgment in the same breath without a new clause.

word_order_figures.name: synchysis
word_order_figures.definition: Interlocked or confused word order in which the natural pairings are woven together.
word_order_figures.example: Cold the morning came, and the men slow.
word_order_figures.effect: Mimics disorder in the ordering of the words themselves.
word_order_figures.caution: Very easily mistaken for a typo in modern prose.

word_order_figures.name: hysteron proteron
word_order_figures.definition: Reversal of the natural or chronological order of two elements.
word_order_figures.example: He was buried and died, as the town told it, in the same week of the same bad winter.
word_order_figures.effect: Puts the consequential event first, which is how memory and rumor actually order things.

word_order_figures.name: anacoluthon
word_order_figures.definition: A break in grammatical sequence, the sentence ending in a construction different from the one it began.
word_order_figures.example: The people who signed those forms, I have never understood how they slept.
word_order_figures.effect: Reproduces the swerve of live thought or agitation.
word_order_figures.caution: Indistinguishable from a mistake unless the surrounding voice is clearly speech-shaped.

word_order_figures.name: catacosmesis
word_order_figures.definition: Ordering words from the greatest to the least in dignity or magnitude.
word_order_figures.example: The governor, the mayor, the county clerk, and the man who unlocked the door all claimed credit.
word_order_figures.effect: Ranks as it lists, so the descent itself makes the comment.

word_order_figures.name: hirmus
word_order_figures.definition: A long suspended construction whose sense is withheld until the closing words.
word_order_figures.example: Although the permits were current, the crew certified, the weather clear, and the drawings approved twice, the wall fell.
word_order_figures.effect: Holds the reader in suspension so the resolution lands with the whole sentence behind it.
word_order_figures.caution: Demands control; a suspension that outlasts the reader's memory collapses into confusion.

word_order_figures.name: epiphrasis
word_order_figures.definition: Addition of a clause or phrase after a sentence has apparently closed.
word_order_figures.example: They finished the job in a week. In a week, and under budget, and nobody has explained how.
word_order_figures.effect: Reopens a closed sentence, which reads as afterthought and often as insinuation.

word_order_figures.name: hypozeuxis
word_order_figures.definition: Giving every clause in a series its own subject and verb rather than sharing one.
word_order_figures.example: The engineer signed. The inspector signed. The owner signed. Nobody looked.
word_order_figures.effect: Weights each member equally and refuses the economy of subordination.

word_order_figures.name: enallage
word_order_figures.definition: Substitution of one grammatical form, case, tense, person, or number for another.
word_order_figures.example: We was told to wait, and wait we done.
word_order_figures.effect: Marks dialect, haste, or intensity by bending the grammar rather than the vocabulary.

word_order_figures.name: antiptosis
word_order_figures.definition: Use of one grammatical case in place of another.
word_order_figures.example: Him that signed it never read it.
word_order_figures.effect: Signals vernacular speech or old formal usage depending on the surrounding register.

word_order_figures.name: anthimeria
word_order_figures.definition: Use of one part of speech as another, most often a noun as a verb.
word_order_figures.example: They committee'd the problem until it aged out.
word_order_figures.effect: Compresses a whole action into one unexpected word.
word_order_figures.caution: Business English is saturated with dead anthimeria; a coinage must earn attention, not merely sound current.

word_order_figures.name: golden line
word_order_figures.definition: A line or clause with two modifiers and two nouns interlocked around a central verb, each modifier separated from its noun.
word_order_figures.example: Slow water over broken stone ran cold.
word_order_figures.effect: Produces a self-consciously wrought symmetry that stops the reader on the sentence itself.
word_order_figures.caution: Latin word order carries this easily; English has to be bent to it, and the bending shows.

word_order_figures.name: heterosis
word_order_figures.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — tense, person, number, or mood — against the sense's normal requirement.
word_order_figures.example: So the inspector walks in, and nobody has looked at that gauge in a year.
word_order_figures.effect: Shifts the temporal or personal footing of a passage without announcing the shift.
word_order_figures.register: informal to neutral; oral narration, free indirect style
word_order_figures.caution: Indistinguishable from a mistake unless the surrounding voice is firmly established.

word_order_figures.name: behaghel's law of increasing terms
word_order_figures.aka: the law of increasing members, end weight
word_order_figures.definition: The principle that coordinate members are best ordered from shortest to longest, so a series ends on its heaviest element.
word_order_figures.example: It cost him the contract, the license, and every professional friendship he had made in thirty years.
word_order_figures.effect: Lets a sentence land instead of trailing off; the ear expects the long member last.
word_order_figures.caution: Violating it deliberately is a legitimate move, but violating it by accident is the commonest cause of a limp sentence.

word_order_figures.name: proleptic accusative
word_order_figures.definition: Pulling the subject of a subordinate clause forward into the main clause, so it is named before the clause that governs it.
word_order_figures.example: I know the gauge, what it was doing that week.
word_order_figures.effect: Gets the important noun into the reader's hands early and leaves the analysis trailing behind it.
word_order_figures.register: informal to neutral; speech, folk narration, scripture
word_order_figures.caution: Modern editors read it as a dangling fragment; keep it in voiced passages.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: paronomasia
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Play on words that sound alike but differ in meaning.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The inspector was thorough about the wrong things: he checked the plans, not the planks.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Yokes two meanings by sound, which reads as wit or as bitter coincidence.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: neutral; commentary, comic and literary prose
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: One pun invites the reader to look for more; a second in the same page turns the piece into a routine.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: asteismus
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Urbane, polite mockery, especially a reply that twists the sense of the previous speaker's word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: They said the process was robust. It was: it survived every attempt to make it work.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Deflects and rebukes at once, without raising the voice.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: charientismus
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Softening a hostile or awkward remark by answering it with a joke.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: You said the roof would hold. It held opinions, mostly.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Defuses aggression while conceding nothing.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: aenigma
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A deliberately obscure allegorical statement whose sense must be worked out.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The house that pays its own taxes will fall on the man who built it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Withholds meaning to make the reader participate in retrieving it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: The line between enigma and unclear writing is the reader's willingness to work; assume less than you would like.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: noema
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A subtle or obscure saying whose point becomes clear only on reflection.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: Every audit finds what it was hired to find.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Rewards attention with a delayed detonation of sense.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: adianoeta
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: An expression carrying an obvious meaning and a second, contrary meaning known to some of the audience.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: No one could have worked harder to keep that report short.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Lets a compliment double as an indictment for the reader who knows.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: double entendre
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A phrase deliberately open to two interpretations, one of them usually improper or damaging.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The firm has always been generous with its own accounts.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Says the acceptable thing while making the unacceptable one audible.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal to neutral; comic prose, satire
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Reads as smirking if the second sense is too available; the best ones can be denied.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: paraprosdokian
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A sentence whose ending reframes the meaning of everything before it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: He had a gift for saving money, chiefly other people's.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Sets an expectation and revokes it in the last few words.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal to neutral; comic prose, aphorism
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: A joke-shaped figure; too many make a serious argument read as stand-up.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: onomatopoeia
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Use of a word whose sound imitates what it names, or the coinage of such a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The pump gulped, then knocked, then quit.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Puts the noise in the reader's mouth rather than describing it.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: neologism
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Coinage of a new word to name something the language has no term for.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The office had a whole practice of pre-blaming: assigning fault in advance of the failure.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Makes a phenomenon nameable and therefore arguable about.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: A coinage must be doing work no existing word does, or it reads as jargon-building.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: acrostic
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A composition in which the initial letters of successive lines or sections spell a word or message.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: A resignation letter whose paragraph initials spelled the name of the department that forced it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Hides a second text inside the first, discovered rather than read.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: anagram
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Rearrangement of the letters of a word or name to form another with pointed relevance.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The firm's slogan rearranged, letter for letter, into a description of its balance sheet.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Suggests that the truth was already latent in the name.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Almost always feels contrived in serious nonfiction.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: tmesis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Separation of the parts of a compound word by an interposed word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: This is a fine how-in-the-world-did-we-get-here do.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Wedges emphasis into the middle of a word, which sounds spoken and vehement.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: prosthesis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Addition of a letter or syllable to the beginning of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: adown the stairs
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Archaizes or stretches the word for meter and mouthfeel.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: aphaeresis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Omission of a letter or syllable from the beginning of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: round the corner, cause he said so
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Clips the word into speech and drops the register a notch.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: epenthesis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Insertion of a letter or syllable into the middle of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: athalete, filum
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Marks dialect or mispronunciation with a single spelling.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: syncope
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Omission of a letter or syllable from the middle of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: ne'er, med'cine, ev'ry
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Compresses a word to fit rhythm or a clipped speaking voice.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: apocope
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Omission of a letter or syllable from the end of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: th' inspector, goin', mornin'
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Shortens the word and slurs the line toward speech.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: paragoge
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Addition of a letter or syllable to the end of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: climbed up the hill-o
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Extends the word for song, dialect, or archaic flavor.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: metathesis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Transposition of letters or sounds within a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: aks for ask; brid for bird
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Fixes a speaker's origin or era in one word.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: antisthecon
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Substitution of one letter or sound for another within a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: wrang for wrong
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Renders accent without resorting to phonetic paragraphs.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Heavy eye-dialect patronizes the speaker; a single substitution per passage is usually enough.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: elision
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Omission of a vowel or syllable at the junction of two words so they run together.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: th'other side; I'm on't now
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Speeds the line and binds two words into one breath.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: abecedarian
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A composition whose successive units begin with the letters of the alphabet in order.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: Audit. Backlog. Culvert. Deferral. The glossary read like an indictment in alphabetical order.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Imposes an arbitrary order that makes an inventory feel exhaustive and slightly inhuman.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: formal; devotional verse, experimental prose, glossary and list forms
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: The constraint eats the content; readers who spot the pattern read for the letters, not the argument.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: telestich
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A composition in which the final letters of successive lines spell out a word or message.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: A poem whose line-endings spell the name of the town the poem never names.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Hides a signature where only a rereading finds it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: formal; verse, puzzle and dedication forms
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Almost invisible in prose; reserve it for lineated text.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: paragram
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A pun made by altering a single letter of a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The county called it a management plan; after the third summer the clerks called it a damage plan.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Delivers a whole judgment in one changed letter, which reads as wit rather than as accusation.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal to neutral; satire, headline, dialogue
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: One letter's distance from mere typo; make the joke unmistakable or cut it.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: spoonerism
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Transposition of the initial sounds of two nearby words.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: He meant to say a well-oiled machine and said a well-boiled mission.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Comic and characterizing; marks fatigue, nerves, or a mind moving faster than a mouth.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Charming once per book; a character who does it twice has a gimmick instead of a voice.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: portmanteau
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A new word made by fusing parts of two existing words along with their meanings.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The office ran on what one clerk called permitigation: permits pursued as a form of litigation.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Names a thing that had no name and carries its own definition inside it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal to neutral; satire, technical coinage, journalism
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Coinages date faster than any other device; a blend that needs a gloss is not yet a word.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: eggcorn
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Substitution of a similar-sounding word or phrase that makes its own plausible sense in place of the standard one.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The foreman wrote that the wall had been a doggy-dog fight against the water since spring.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Reveals how a speaker has reasoned their way to a phrase; funnier and gentler than a malapropism.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: In the writer's own voice it is simply an error, and the reader will not credit you with the joke.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: mondegreen
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A mishearing of a spoken or sung phrase that reanalyzes it into different words.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: For years he thought the hymn asked mercy for the gladly cross-eyed bear.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Turns an error of hearing into an image, and often into a memory more durable than the original.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: palindrome
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A word, phrase, or passage that reads the same forward and backward.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: Never odd or even, said the auditor, which was the only joke he made that year.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Displays craft for its own sake and makes a phrase feel machined rather than spoken.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal to formal; puzzle forms, ornamental prose
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Pure ornament: it almost never says the thing you actually need said.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: lipogram
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A composition that deliberately excludes a letter of the alphabet throughout.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: A chapter about the drowning written without the letter that begins the drowned town's name.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Makes an absence structural, so form enacts what the content withholds.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: The vocabulary the constraint forbids is usually the vocabulary the subject needs.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: chronogram
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A phrase in which certain letters, read as Roman numerals, sum to a significant date.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: A cornerstone motto whose capitals add to the year the levee was finished.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Buries a date in a sentence so that the inscription is also a record.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: formal; inscriptions, dedications, historical set pieces
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Invisible without a gloss, and a gloss kills it; useful chiefly as a described artifact.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: wellerism
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: A saying completed by an attribution and a situation that recast it, usually with grim comedy.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: Everything is under control, as the man said with one foot on the dock and one on the boat.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Puts a proverb and its refutation in the same sentence.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal; dialogue, folk narration, comic aside
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: A period flavor; used straight in modern prose it reads as pastiche.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: rebus
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Representation of a word or phrase by pictures or letters that stand for its sounds.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The children's map marked the flooded field with an eye, a heart, and a drawing of the culvert.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Forces the reader to decode rather than read, which slows attention to the sign itself.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: informal; children's forms, puzzle, described artifact

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: synaeresis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Contraction of two adjacent vowels into a single syllable within a word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: Saying seest as one syllable to keep the line's count.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Buys a syllable back where the meter or the cadence needs it.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.register: formal; verse, archaic and liturgical prose
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Marks a text as period work; in contemporary prose it looks like a typo.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: ecthlipsis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Elision of a final consonant — classically Latin final m — before a following vowel.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: Reading multum ille as multill' in the scansion of a hexameter.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Smooths a junction that would otherwise clot the line.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: A technical term for reading verse, not a device to deploy in English prose.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: crasis
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Fusion of the final vowel of one word with the initial vowel of the next into a single sound.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: The clerk's the one who noticed, run together in speech until it is one word.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Compresses speech toward how it is actually said.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: Heavy phonetic spelling patronizes the speaker; use the lightest mark that carries the sound.

wordplay_and_word_form_figures.name: reduplication
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.definition: Repeating a word or its skeleton, often with a vowel or consonant change, to mark intensity, dismissal, or a stricter sense.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.example: It was not an inspection inspection. It was a man walking past a gauge.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.effect: Lets ordinary words carry emphasis or scorn without a modifier.
wordplay_and_word_form_figures.caution: A spoken construction; on the page it needs a voice around it or it reads as an error.

metaphor_family.name: metaphor
metaphor_family.definition: Application of a word or image to something it does not literally denote, asserting identity rather than likeness.
metaphor_family.example: The committee was a sieve; every decision passed through it and none stayed.
metaphor_family.effect: Imports the structure of one domain into another so the reader understands by transfer.
metaphor_family.caution: Mixed, stacked, or stock metaphors are the fastest route to slop; one live metaphor beats four dead ones.

metaphor_family.name: conceptual metaphor
metaphor_family.definition: An underlying metaphorical mapping that organizes a whole family of ordinary expressions.
metaphor_family.example: Argument as war: he attacked the premise, defended his position, and lost ground on the third point.
metaphor_family.effect: Shapes reasoning below the level of style, since the mapping smuggles in its own entailments.
metaphor_family.caution: Because it is invisible, it decides what the argument can say; check which entailments you have accepted.

metaphor_family.name: extended metaphor
metaphor_family.definition: A metaphor sustained and developed across several sentences or a whole passage.
metaphor_family.example: The budget was a tide chart. It told you when the water would leave, not why the boats were rotten.
metaphor_family.effect: Lets a comparison do structural work instead of decorating a single clause.
metaphor_family.caution: Every added term must still fit the source domain; extension is where metaphors go mixed.

metaphor_family.name: submerged metaphor
metaphor_family.definition: A metaphor whose vehicle is implied by a single word rather than stated.
metaphor_family.example: The proposal limped through three committees.
metaphor_family.effect: Puts the image in the verb, where the reader absorbs it without pausing.

metaphor_family.name: dead metaphor
metaphor_family.definition: A metaphor so worn by use that its image is no longer felt.
metaphor_family.example: the leg of the table; the heart of the matter
metaphor_family.effect: Functions as plain vocabulary; harmless alone, deadening when a passage runs on nothing else.
metaphor_family.caution: Waking a dead metaphor by accident produces comedy: the heart of the matter beat faster.

metaphor_family.name: mixed metaphor
metaphor_family.definition: Combination of two or more incompatible metaphorical images in one construction.
metaphor_family.example: We will iron out the bottlenecks before they snowball.
metaphor_family.effect: Almost always a fault; used knowingly it characterizes a speaker who talks in borrowed phrases.
metaphor_family.caution: A reliable symptom of stitched-together prose; hunt for it wherever two clauses each carry an image.

metaphor_family.name: catachresis
metaphor_family.definition: Deliberate misapplication of a word to a thing that has no proper name of its own, or a wrenching metaphor.
metaphor_family.example: the mouth of the river; a blind window; to shoulder the blame
metaphor_family.effect: Fills a lexical gap or forces a violent, memorable transfer.
metaphor_family.caution: Wrenched metaphor is a fine line from nonsense; the reader must feel the strain as intended.

metaphor_family.name: conceit
metaphor_family.definition: An elaborate, sustained, and often startling comparison between wildly unlike things.
metaphor_family.example: A pension fund is a promise kept in a language its makers will not live to speak.
metaphor_family.effect: Draws attention to its own ingenuity and asks the reader to be impressed and convinced at once.
metaphor_family.caution: The most flattering figure to write and the least forgiving to read; a failed conceit sinks a page.

metaphor_family.name: simile
metaphor_family.definition: Explicit comparison of two unlike things using like, as, or a comparative frame.
metaphor_family.example: The ledger read like a diary kept by someone with something to hide.
metaphor_family.effect: States the comparison openly, which is clearer and cooler than metaphor.
metaphor_family.caution: Stacked similes are an AI tell; if two arrive in a paragraph, one is decoration.

metaphor_family.name: epic simile
metaphor_family.definition: An extended simile whose vehicle is developed into a miniature scene before returning to the tenor.
metaphor_family.example: As a man who has walked all night keeps walking because stopping means feeling his feet, so the department kept auditing.
metaphor_family.effect: Suspends the narrative to open a second world, then folds it back with the comparison earned.
metaphor_family.caution: Costly in attention; one per chapter at the outside.

metaphor_family.name: parabola
metaphor_family.definition: A comparison drawn out as a short fictional narrative that carries a transferable lesson.
metaphor_family.example: A man rebuilt his fence each spring where the river had taken it, and each spring called the river treacherous.
metaphor_family.effect: Delivers a moral by illustration, letting the reader arrive at the claim unprompted.

metaphor_family.name: analogy
metaphor_family.definition: Figure sense: a proportional comparison asserting that one pair of terms relates as another pair does. Distinct from the evidential analogy, whose worth is measured by the correspondence itself.
metaphor_family.example: An audit is to a company what a mirror is to a face that has been avoiding mirrors.
metaphor_family.effect: Transfers a relation rather than an image, which makes it usable as an argument.
metaphor_family.caution: Analogy persuades faster than it proves; expect the reader to attack the disanalogy.

metaphor_family.name: allegory
metaphor_family.definition: A sustained metaphor in which the entire surface narrative stands for a second, coherent set of referents.
metaphor_family.example: A story about a lighthouse keeper who refuses to change the bulb, told as the history of a regulatory agency.
metaphor_family.effect: Lets the reader hold two stories at once and applies the moral without naming the target.

metaphor_family.name: personification
metaphor_family.definition: Attribution of human qualities, agency, or feeling to an animal, object, or abstraction.
metaphor_family.example: The building had learned to hide its cracks behind new paint.
metaphor_family.effect: Gives an abstraction a will, which makes it a character the reader can hold responsible.
metaphor_family.caution: Institutions that yearn and markets that feel are a stock move of inflated prose; use only when agency is the point.

metaphor_family.name: antiprosopopoeia
metaphor_family.definition: The reverse of personification: representing a person as an inanimate thing.
metaphor_family.example: By the third year he was a fixture in the lobby, a coat rack with opinions.
metaphor_family.effect: Strips agency from a person, producing pathos or contempt.

metaphor_family.name: anthropomorphism
metaphor_family.definition: Representation of a nonhuman being or force as literally having a human form or mind.
metaphor_family.example: The river, in their telling, chose the west channel out of spite.
metaphor_family.effect: Converts process into intention, which explains vividly and misleads easily.
metaphor_family.caution: In explanatory nonfiction it can install a false causal story; flag it as a figure when you use it.

metaphor_family.name: zoomorphism
metaphor_family.definition: Attribution of animal characteristics to a person, deity, or object.
metaphor_family.example: He came into meetings the way a heron comes to a shallow: still, then sudden.
metaphor_family.effect: Characterizes by species-behavior, which is faster than psychology.

metaphor_family.name: pathetic fallacy
metaphor_family.definition: Attribution of human emotion to nature, especially weather, in sympathy with a scene.
metaphor_family.example: The sky went sullen over the courthouse.
metaphor_family.effect: Aligns setting with feeling so the landscape does some of the emotional work.
metaphor_family.caution: Storm-at-the-funeral is the cheapest version; once per book, and never at the climax.

metaphor_family.name: synaesthesia
metaphor_family.definition: Description of one sensory experience in terms proper to another.
metaphor_family.example: a sour green light over the loading dock
metaphor_family.effect: Produces an impression no single-sense description can, and marks a heightened perceptual state.
metaphor_family.caution: A signature of over-written description; two per chapter is already a lot.

metaphor_family.name: kenning
metaphor_family.definition: A compressed, formulaic metaphorical compound used in place of a plain noun.
metaphor_family.example: paper-weather for the season of audits; wound-tide for blood
metaphor_family.effect: Renames a common thing so it recovers strangeness.
